description: PathValidationResult — per-link measurement (spec/07-routing.md §4): source_id, next_hop_id, destination_id, measured_rtt_ms, measured_loss_pct, valid_until, and the source's Ed25519 signature over the canonical encoding of the other fields. Every hex value below is derived from the REAL reference implementation in reference/routing/path-validation.ts (createPathValidationResult / encodePathValidationBody / pathValidationSigningPayload / verifyPathValidationResult / encodePathValidationWire). The source keypair is derived deterministically from a 32-byte test seed (sharedKeys.sourceSeedHex) via keypairFromSecretKey, so the vector is byte-stable and reproducible.
statusNote: FROZEN — every hex value is generated by the real reference implementation (reference/routing/path-validation.ts). The source keypair is derived deterministically from sharedKeys.sourceSeedHex via keypairFromSecretKey. Mutating any body field (source_id, next_hop_id, destination_id, measured_rtt_ms, measured_loss_pct, valid_until) invalidates the signature. Mutating the signature field (or the public key) breaks verification. Both the TS runner and the independent Python verifier reproduce these exact bytes.

constants.bodyEncoding: canonical CBOR (RFC 8949 §4.2.2), integer-keyed map per ADR-0004

bodyMapKeys.2: next_hop_id (text, NodeId of the next hop)
bodyMapKeys.4: measured_rtt_ms (uint, measured round-trip time in milliseconds)
bodyMapKeys.5: measured_loss_pct (uint, measured packet loss as a percentage 0-100)
bodyMapKeys.6: valid_until (uint, unix seconds — when this measurement expires)
bodyMapKeys.7: signature (bstr .size 64, Ed25519 by source over the canonical encoding of keys 1-6)

constants.note: Field names use snake_case (source_id, next_hop_id, destination_id, measured_rtt_ms, measured_loss_pct, valid_until) per spec/07 §4 wire-object declaration, mirroring the spec's prose. The integer keys (1-7) follow ADR-0004.

sharedKeys.note: Source keypair derived deterministically from sourceSeedHex via keypairFromSecretKey (reference/identity/keys.ts). The seed is committed here so the vector is reproducible end-to-end. The next-hop and destination NodeIds are stable test NodeIds (canonical 52-char base32) — only the source's signature is verified, so they do not need to be bound to real keypairs.

vectors.name: valid-path-validation
vectors.description: A source node measures RTT=42ms and loss=1% on the link to a next-hop toward the destination. The source signs the canonical encoding of the measurement (fields 1-6) using createPathValidationResult(body, sourceSecretKey). verifyPathValidationResult(result, sourcePublicKey) returns true. The full PathValidationResult wire object (fields 1-7, including the signature as field 7) is captured as wireHex via encodePathValidationWire(result).

verification: Reference implementation: reference/routing/path-validation.ts. Hex values are generated by: createPathValidationResult (signature), encodePathValidationBody (bodyHex), pathValidationSigningPayload (signingPayloadHex), verifyPathValidationResult (verificationResult=ok), encodePathValidationWire (wireHex). The source keypair is derived via keypairFromSecretKey(sharedKeys.sourceSeedHex) in reference/identity/keys.ts. An independent Python verifier (conformance/runners/py_vector_verifier.py::verify_path_validation_vector) reproduces these exact bytes from scratch using cbor2 + PyNaCl.
notes: Per spec/07 §4: Path Validation is per-link, not end-to-end — the source accumulates PathValidationResults for each hop in the candidate path. The result is signed by the SOURCE (not the next-hop), as it is the source's measurement. The domain tag SHARENET/PATH/VALIDATION/1 is registered in spec/14-security.md §4 and exposed as PATH_VALIDATION_DOMAIN in the reference implementation. The integer-keyed CBOR map follows ADR-0004.
